text:
Priya Rao: Heads-up — we received a deletion request from an EU customer asking us to remove their raw data and any derived embeddings. They included a KMS key ARN and claim some nightly backups may contain their vectors. Can infra/security take a look?

Alex Kim: Paste the request and key ARN here, please. We'll check KMS access logs + S3 snapshots.

Priya Rao: customer: acme-eu; subject_id: 8421; kms_key: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01; request attached (signed).

Samir Patel: Noted. This customer is on our Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed KMS). Important: the key looks to be customer-owned (cross-account). We might not have decrypt access. We only store encrypted pointers for embeddings if the customer uses their KMS.

InfraBot: audit: No decrypt calls for arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01 from our prod account in the last 90 days. (query id: audit-q-9203) :mag:

Alex Kim: That suggests we didn't interact with their KMS directly, but embeddings could still be in our faiss index with a subject tag. I can query the index metadata for subject_id=8421.

Jordan (eng-security): Current RBAC prevents the privacy service from issuing delete operations against vector indices. The service account only has vector-reader. We'll need a scoped privilege 'privacy-delete' to perform deletions safely.

Marta Lopez: I can run the deletion job but need a short-lived elevation. Proposal: create a scoped grant 'privacy-delete-1765' limited to index=faiss-prod-eu and TTL=2h. Approve? :lock:

Priya Rao: Legal flagged potential legal hold. We should request a retention exception until legal confirms (we may need to preserve evidence). @Legal Bot can you confirm the hold status for subject_id 8421?

Legal Bot: Received INFSEC request INFSEC-4821. Legal needs a custody and litigation check — please attach any forensic artifacts (S3 access logs, KMS audit ids, index deletion plan). Will respond within 24h.

Samir Patel: While investigating I found an S3 snapshot prefix that contains a shard tagged with subject=8421: s3://redwood-backups/prod/faiss/2025-11-12/part-0004. If we delete that blob we must ensure it doesn't break cross-region restores. Suggest we copy->redact->verify -> then remove original.

Alex Kim: Suggested dry-run command for infra ops:
```
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-backups/prod/faiss/2025-11-12/part-0004 --profile infra --dryrun
```
We'll follow with an actual remove only after legal signoff and restore verification.

Priya Rao: Also we need to run KMS + S3 access log queries to confirm there was no unauthorized access before our patch last quarter. That ties into vuln triage — any exfil window?

Samir Patel: We patched S3 snapshot access (CVE-2025-xxxx) in December. Need to run access-log scan for 90 days pre-patch. I'll open a vuln-triage ticket and attach results.

Marta Lopez: Starting a dry-run of the deletion script against faiss-prod-eu: `./scripts/redact_embeddings.py --index faiss-prod-eu --subject 8421 --dry-run`
Dry-run result: 312 vectors matched, 14 doc references. No integrity errors.

Alex Kim: Good. Approve deletion once Legal clears. Please snapshot the pre-delete sha256 and include audit id in the ticket.

InfraBot: created grant privacy-delete-1765 for service-account privacy-service, scope:index=faiss-prod-eu, expires_at=1765010676, audit_id=audit-pt-875. :white_check_mark:

Priya Rao: Thanks. I've assigned INFSEC-4821 to @Marta Lopez and added audit-pt-875 + dry-run output. Legal, please confirm hold status — if no hold, Marta will run deletion; if hold, we'll request a retention exception window and proceed with a redaction-preserve workflow. :eyes: :thumbsup:

Legal Bot: Acknowledged. Legal will confirm hold/no-hold by EOD and advise on retention-exception timeframe if needed (likely 30–90 days). Please keep all artifacts immutable until we respond.

Jordan (eng-security): Post-actions: 1) record deletion audit event with id  — include pre-delete hashes. 2) rotate any associated keys if cross-account access was used. 3) update RBAC docs to make short-lived privacy-delete grants a standard pattern.

Marta Lopez: Understood. Will not execute destructive ops until Legal OK. Dry-run logs and sha256 snapshots uploaded to INFSEC-4821. Starting monitoring queries for S3 access and KMS decrypts now.

Priya Rao: Thanks team. I'll follow up in the ticket and post a summary in #privacy-updates after Legal responds.
